items.label: f01-presigned-url
items.front: What is SigV4 presigning, and what can the holder of a presigned URL do?
items.back: The server computes a signature over the one request it wants to authorise and embeds it in the query string (X-Amz-Signature, -Credential, -Date, -Expires). The holder can make that one request until expiresIn elapses, and nothing else; the secret key never leaves the server.

items.label: f03-v1-v2-exercise
items.front: Why are elihyper2's v2 unit tests (cd app && npm test) runnable without AWS credentials, and what does that tell you?
items.back: v2 builds the Express app with injected AWS clients, so tests (plain node --test) pass fake Polly/Claude stand-ins (createFakePolly, createFakeClaude) and assert e.g. GET /health never touches AWS. The AWS calls live behind injected dependencies at the edge, not inside the logic under test.

items.label: f02-cors-budget-drain
items.front: nova-bpt v1 issue 6.2: app.use(cors()) on credential-backed endpoints. Why is it high severity before any deployment?
items.back: cors() with no options allows any origin, and /get-signed-url hands out direct AWS access with no auth and no rate limit, so one link click on any site can drain the AWS budget. STORY-04 locks down CORS and adds rate limiting.

items.prompt: In nova-bpt v1, how does the trust pattern of /get-signed-url differ from /speak and /ask-claude?

choices.text: It is a credential broker: the server signs a URL and the browser then talks to AWS directly, without the server
It is a proxy too, relaying every audio chunk through the server
It sends the AWS secret key to the browser for five minutes
It is the only endpoint that requires an authenticated user

choices: It is a credential broker: the server signs a URL and the browser then talks to AWS directly, without the server
It is a proxy too, relaying every audio chunk through the server
It sends the AWS secret key to the browser for five minutes
It is the only endpoint that requires an authenticated user

items.explanation: '/speak and /ask-claude are a proxy... /get-signed-url is a credential broker. The server signs a URL and hands it over; the browser then talks to AWS directly over a WebSocket.'

items.prompt: v1 uses express.static('public'). You start the server from the parent directory. What happens to the HTML pages?

choices.text: The server refuses to start because the folder is missing
Express falls back to serving the files from node_modules
They load normally, because Express resolves paths relative to the entry file
They silently 404, because the path resolves against the working directory, not server.js

choices: The server refuses to start because the folder is missing
Express falls back to serving the files from node_modules
They load normally, because Express resolves paths relative to the entry file
They silently 404, because the path resolves against the working directory, not server.js

items.explanation: 'express.static('public') resolves relative to the process working directory, not to server.js... Prefer express.static(path.join(__dirname, 'public')).'

items.prompt: In an AWS event-stream audio frame, which part is little-endian?

choices.text: Only the PCM samples inside the payload; the lengths and header fields are big-endian
Everything, because Web Audio produces little-endian Float32 data
Only the two CRC32 checksums at the prelude and end
Only the total-length and headers-length prelude fields

choices: Only the PCM samples inside the payload; the lengths and header fields are big-endian
Everything, because Web Audio produces little-endian Float32 data
Only the two CRC32 checksums at the prelude and end
Only the total-length and headers-length prelude fields

items.explanation: 'Everything here is big-endian except the PCM samples inside the payload, which are little-endian. Mixing those up is the classic bug in this code path.'

items.prompt: What does hoisting new PollyClient(...) out of the /speak handler to module scope buy?

choices.text: It is required for AudioStream.pipe(res) to stream
The SDK can reuse its client, credential resolver and connections instead of rebuilding them every request
It lets Polly accept more than 3000 characters per call
It makes the voice and engine configurable per request

choices: It is required for AudioStream.pipe(res) to stream
The SDK can reuse its client, credential resolver and connections instead of rebuilding them every request
It lets Polly accept more than 3000 characters per call
It makes the voice and engine configurable per request

items.explanation: The in-handler client 'builds a fresh client, credential resolver and HTTP agent on every request. Hoisting it to module scope is a one-line change and lets the SDK reuse connections.'

items.prompt: The presigner is configured with service: "transcribestreaming" to match the hostname. What is the symptom?

choices.text: Nothing: SigV4 accepts either service name for Transcribe
The URL expires immediately instead of after five minutes
An opaque 403 when the WebSocket connects, because the signing service name must be transcribe
A DNS failure, because the hostname is rebuilt from the service name

choices: Nothing: SigV4 accepts either service name for Transcribe
The URL expires immediately instead of after five minutes
An opaque 403 when the WebSocket connects, because the signing service name must be transcribe
A DNS failure, because the hostname is rebuilt from the service name

items.explanation: 'service: "transcribe" — not "transcribestreaming". The signing service name and the hostname prefix differ. Getting this wrong produces an opaque 403 on WebSocket connect.'

items.prompt: In v1, a user types 'what is 2+2' into claude.html. Why do they see 'Error.'?

choices.text: The server JSON.parses the prompt string as a messages array, which throws and returns a 500
CORS blocks the request because claude.html sets no origin
Bedrock rejects prompts shorter than ten characters
The Claude model ID had expired and Bedrock returned 404

choices: The server JSON.parses the prompt string as a messages array, which throws and returns a 500
CORS blocks the request because claude.html sets no origin
Bedrock rejects prompts shorter than ten characters
The Claude model ID had expired and Bedrock returned 404

items.explanation: claude.html sends { prompt: input } as a raw string; server.js does JSON.parse(req.body.prompt), which throws for 'what is 2+2'; the catch returns 500 and the page renders 'Error.'. A contract regression from commit f8dba37.

items.prompt: Why are the x-amzn-transcribe-* headers excluded from the SigV4 presign signature?

choices.text: They contain the secret key, which must never be signed
Excluding them makes the URL shorter than the browser's limit
A browser WebSocket cannot send custom headers, so signing them would never match; query parameters do the real work
AWS forbids signing any header that starts with x-amzn

choices: They contain the secret key, which must never be signed
Excluding them makes the URL shorter than the browser's limit
A browser WebSocket cannot send custom headers, so signing them would never match; query parameters do the real work
AWS forbids signing any header that starts with x-amzn

items.explanation: 'a browser WebSocket cannot send custom headers. If they were signed, the signature would never match what the browser actually sends.'

items.prompt: A Transcribe result arrives with IsPartial: true. How should the page treat it?

choices.text: As an error frame that should close the WebSocket
As final text, since Transcribe only sends confident results
As a running guess that will be replaced, not appended to the final transcript
As a duplicate of the previous final result, to be discarded

choices: As an error frame that should close the WebSocket
As final text, since Transcribe only sends confident results
As a running guess that will be replaced, not appended to the final transcript
As a duplicate of the previous final result, to be discarded

items.explanation: 'IsPartial: true means "this will change"... IsPartial: false means "this is settled" — the code appends it to the output.'

items.prompt: Why does v1 broker a signed URL for Transcribe instead of proxying the stream, and what is the cost?

choices.text: Browsers cannot open WebSockets to localhost; the cost is a second TLS handshake
Proxying a long-lived audio stream means relaying every chunk; the cost is that anyone reaching the endpoint gets five minutes of unmetered AWS access
Transcribe rejects server IPs; the cost is that captions arrive out of order
Signed URLs are cheaper on AWS billing; the cost is losing partial results

choices: Browsers cannot open WebSockets to localhost; the cost is a second TLS handshake
Proxying a long-lived audio stream means relaying every chunk; the cost is that anyone reaching the endpoint gets five minutes of unmetered AWS access
Transcribe rejects server IPs; the cost is that captions arrive out of order
Signed URLs are cheaper on AWS billing; the cost is losing partial results

items.explanation: Transcribe streaming is long-lived and bidirectional; brokering is simpler and lower latency. 'The tradeoff is that anyone who can reach /get-signed-url gets five minutes of direct, unmetered access.'

items.prompt: Why is an async onaudioprocess handler that awaits resampling before socket.send() dangerous?

choices.text: Awaiting inside the handler blocks the WebSocket from receiving events
Callbacks fire on a fixed cadence without waiting, so two in flight can send audio out of order
Resampling changes the endianness of the PCM samples
The handler runs only once because async callbacks are not re-entrant

choices: Awaiting inside the handler blocks the WebSocket from receiving events
Callbacks fire on a fixed cadence without waiting, so two in flight can send audio out of order
Resampling changes the endianness of the PCM samples
The handler runs only once because async callbacks are not re-entrant

items.explanation: 'onaudioprocess fires on a fixed cadence and does not wait for the previous promise. If two callbacks are ever in flight, their socket.send() calls can land out of order.' Rare, and 'rarely is the worst kind of bug.'

items.prompt: The v1 /ask-claude handler returns responseBody.content[0].text. What assumption is that line making?

choices.text: That content is a string rather than an array
That the first content block is a text block, which holds for a plain reply but is load-bearing
That the anthropic_version field names the model version
That the model always returns exactly one token

choices: That content is a string rather than an array
That the first content block is a text block, which holds for a plain reply but is load-bearing
That the anthropic_version field names the model version
That the model always returns exactly one token

items.explanation: 'responseBody.content is an array of content blocks, and the code assumes content[0] is a text block. That is true for a plain text reply, but it is a load-bearing assumption.'
